description: Command injection vulnerability in shell-exec. The command is wrapped in double quotes and passed to /bin/sh -c. Scheme's ~s (write) does not escape shell metacharacters like $, `, and \ inside strings, allowing an attacker to execute arbitrary commands using command substitution (e.g., $(reboot)).
code_snippet:
(let* ([wrapped-cmd (format "/bin/sh -c ~s'; echo \"\\n__EXIT_CODE__$?\"'" cmd)])
               (let-values ([(to-stdin from-stdout from-stderr process-id)
                             (open-process-ports wrapped-cmd
                                                 (buffer-mode block)
                                                 (native-transcoder))])
suggested_fix: Use single quotes for the command argument and escape any single quotes within the command string, or better, avoid shell execution and use a list of arguments with a direct process execution function if available.

description: Command injection in beads effect handler. The 'type' and 'priority' fields are inserted into a shell command string using ~a (display), which performs no escaping. This allows an attacker who controls these values to execute arbitrary shell commands.
code_snippet:
(let* ([title (cadr payload)]
                     [description (caddr payload)]
                     [type (cadddr payload)]
                     [priority (list-ref payload 4)]
                     [cmd (format "bd create ~s -d ~s -t ~a -p ~a"
                                  title description type priority)]
                     [result (shell-exec cmd)])
suggested_fix: Use ~s for all parameters and ensure shell-exec properly handles escaping of shell metacharacters.

description: Path traversal vulnerability in fold-ipc-eval. The session-id is used directly to construct file paths for IPC. If session-id is user-controllable, an attacker can use '..' sequences to write or delete files outside the intended directories.
code_snippet:
(let ([req-path (string-append req-dir "/" session-id ".ss")]
                    [resp-path (string-append resp-dir "/" session-id ".txt")])
                   ;; Clear any stale response
                   (when (file-exists? resp-path)
                         (delete-file resp-path))
suggested_fix: Sanitize session-id to ensure it only contains alphanumeric characters and no path separators or '..' sequences.

description: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability. The http-fetch-get function passes a user-provided URL directly to curl without validation, allowing access to internal network services or local files via the file:// protocol.
suggested_fix: Validate the URL against an allowlist of permitted protocols (e.g., http, https) and domains, and block access to private/internal IP ranges.

description: Path traversal in checkpoint persistence. The run-id and name are used to construct file paths for checkpoint storage. If these are user-controlled, an attacker can write arbitrary S-expression files to any location on the filesystem.
code_snippet:
(define (persist-checkpoint run-id name value)
  (guard (ex [else (void)])
         (let ([run-dir (string-append *checkpoint-dir* "/" run-id)])
              (ensure-directory! run-dir)
              (let ([checkpoint-file (string-append run-dir "/" (symbol->string name) ".sexp")])
suggested_fix: Sanitize run-id and name to prevent path traversal sequences and ensure they remain within the *checkpoint-dir*.

description: Scheme injection in forum-post effect. The channel parameter is inserted into a Scheme expression using ~a, allowing an attacker to break out of the quoted symbol and execute arbitrary Scheme code in the Fold REPL.
code_snippet:
[(forum-post)
              (let* ([channel (cadr payload)]
                     [title (caddr payload)]
                     [body (cadddr payload)]
                     [expr (format "(msg '~a ~s ~s)" channel title body)]
suggested_fix: Use ~s for the channel or validate that it is a valid symbol string containing no Scheme metacharacters like spaces or parentheses.

description: Command injection in shell-exec-with-env. Environment variable values are inserted using ~s into a string that is then executed by /bin/sh -c. Since ~s does not escape shell metacharacters like $ within double quotes, an attacker can execute commands via variable expansion.
code_snippet:
(let* ([env-exports (apply string-append
                                    (map (lambda (pair)
                                                 ;; Use ~s (write) to get proper shell escaping
                                                 (format "export ~a=~s; " (car pair) (cdr pair)))
                                         env))]
                [full-cmd (string-append env-exports cmd "; echo \"\\n__EXIT_CODE__$?\"")])
suggested_fix: Use a safer method for setting environment variables, such as passing them directly to the process creation function, or use single quotes for the export values and escape any internal single quotes.
